what: The industry-standard delivery pattern for closed-source Node CLIs is "thin npm wrapper + binary downloaded from elsewhere" (GitHub Releases, CDN, S3). Users run `npm install -g`, postinstall fetches platform binary, symlinks CLI. Examples all ship this way: Cypress, Playwright, Sentry CLI, Snyk CLI, Prisma CLI, esbuild, swc, Turbo, Biome, Rspack, Rolldown, lightningcss, DataDog CI. The plan's Phase 4 already specifies this pattern. The orthogonal decision is what the binary itself is compiled with — and the modern direction for new serious CLIs that care about BOTH protection and performance is Rust core (via napi-rs or standalone binary) + thin TS wrapper + npm distribution. That's what Turbo / swc / Biome / Rspack / Rolldown / lightningcss all do. If aide-memory ever needs stronger protection than yao-pkg bytecode gives, the idiomatic upgrade path is "port the sensitive module(s) to Rust napi-rs", not "find a stronger JS bundler".
why: Research this turn established the delivery pattern is already standardized (Phase 4 is correct). The actual open decision is only the COMPILER choice, and the modern trajectory for serious tools is Rust N-API. Memory 138 covers protection levels but not this trajectory framing — future binary-migration decisions benefit from seeing the Rust-core + TS-wrapper pattern as the upgrade path rather than looking for yet another pure-JS bundler.
